canonical_refs.note: Locks visual tokens, motion params, banned patterns, a11y rules. Section 17 defines hex palette, typography, spring physics, skeleton timing, banned patterns. Section 18 defines redundant-cue rules.
Mobile-first PWA, tablet-width centered on desktop, pt-BR only, WCAG AA = ship blocker, adapter boundaries.
5 success criteria define ship contract — installable PWA, theme switch, skeletons, placeholder primitives, app-update toast + design-system lint.
D-13 Serwist skeleton-only (Phase 3 must finish offline strategy); D-14 manifest placeholder (Phase 3 rewrites with brand assets); D-15 next-intl as-needed prefix; D-22 Sentry scrub posture.
Phase 3 placeholder pages do not yet exercise repositories or routes — but API conventions inform the diagnostics ping used by offline-banner heartbeat.
next-intl 4.9.1, Next 16.2.3, React 19.2.5, Serwist 9.5.7. Bottom-nav only, max 5 tabs (MVP uses 4). pt-BR only at launch. <html lang='pt-BR'>. date-fns-tz for server-rendered user-local times.

claude_discretion.rationale: PRD §17 locks the markup (<i lang='la'>) and styling (italic Plus Jakarta Sans 14 Calm/Lantern Slate). Component lives at src/shared/typography/scientific-name.tsx; first consumed by Phase 5/6.

src/shared/i18n/format.ts exporting formatCurrencyBRL, formatDate, formatTime, formatDateTime via Intl.* with pt-BR locale + User.timezone injection point. date-fns-tz used per CLAUDE.md for server-rendered user-local times only.
Inline SVG components with currentColor + stroke-width: 1.5px. Theme-aware via CSS color variable. Only theme-aware route.
Same Paper Cream / Night Cream as container — invisible boundary. Locked by 'Folhário is ONE shape across devices' from PRD §17.

questions.title: CSS framework choice
questions.context: Phase 1 didn't pick a CSS solution — src/app/globals.css is empty. Next 16 supports Tailwind v4 first-class via @tailwindcss/postcss. Choose once for the whole app — Phase 5+ feature phases all depend on this. PRD §17's token-heavy spec pairs naturally with Tailwind v4's @theme directive.

options.label: Tailwind CSS v4
options.description: Recommended. Utility classes + @theme for tokens. Mature ecosystem; fastest route from PRD spec to working UI. PRD banned-patterns map to eslint-plugin-tailwindcss + stylelint rules. CSS-first config keeps tokens single-source.

options.label: CSS Modules + CSS variables
options.description: Vanilla. Tokens in globals.css :root + [data-theme=dark]. Per-component .module.css. More verbose but zero runtime, full control, no framework lock-in.

options.label: Panda CSS / Vanilla Extract
options.description: Type-safe build-time CSS-in-JS. Token-aware. More setup; smaller community than Tailwind; more rigorous type contracts.

options.label: Hybrid: Tailwind v4 utility + CSS Modules for complex pieces
options.description: Pragmatic middle ground. Tailwind for 90% utility, modules for skeleton shimmer / motion primitives that need named keyframes.

options.label: Custom (specify in chat-more)

questions.title: Token storage approach
questions.context: PRD §17 has 11 light + 11 dark color tokens, type scale, spring params, 8pt grid. Tokens must be readable from CSS (component styles) AND from JS (motion library reads spring config). Phase 1 set no token convention.

options.label: CSS custom properties in globals.css + JS mirror in src/shared/theme/tokens.ts
options.description: Recommended. :root + [data-theme=dark] for runtime; tokens.ts re-exports the same values for motion lib + JS consumers. Single source of truth via shared constants. Works regardless of CSS framework choice.

options.label: Tailwind v4 @theme directive only (CSS-first config) + theme() in JS
options.description: Minimal duplication; depends on Tailwind v4. Loses dark mode dynamics if Tailwind needs static values for some utilities.

options.label: Style Dictionary multi-output build
options.description: Multi-output (CSS + JS + JSON). Useful if native app comes later. Adds a build step + extra dependency.

options.label: Hybrid: CSS vars for runtime + JS constants only for motion params
options.description: Pragmatic. Motion params don't change at runtime so they don't need CSS-var indirection.

questions.title: Theme attribute placement on <html>
questions.context: Where the dark-mode switch lives in the DOM. Affects every CSS rule's variant syntax. Tailwind v4 supports both class and attribute via @variant dark { … }. data-attribute is CSS-native and framework-agnostic.

options.label: <html data-theme='light|dark|auto'>
options.description: Recommended. Semantic, matches [data-theme=dark] selector pattern; works with any CSS framework; survives framework swaps. For auto, SSR must not guess prefers-color-scheme; CSS media queries resolve the effective light/dark tokens.

options.label: <html class='dark'>
options.description: Tailwind's classic convention. Couples to Tailwind syntax.

options.label: Browser-managed only via prefers-color-scheme
options.description: No manual override path. Conflicts with PRD §17 'Manual override in Settings'.

questions.title: Font loading strategy
questions.context: Source Serif 4 + Plus Jakarta Sans both Google Fonts. PWA must work offline → fonts must self-host + cache. PRD demands variable fonts, +2% tracking on buttons, latin-ext subset for pt-BR diacritics (ã, ç, é).

options.label: next/font/google with subsetting (['latin', 'latin-ext'])
options.description: Recommended. Auto self-hosting, font-display swap baked in. Built into Next 16. Service worker caches statically. Variable axis exposed via weight ranges.

options.label: Self-host downloaded woff2 + next/font/local
options.description: Full control over file paths, version pinning, no Google CDN call. Requires manual variable-font subsetting (glyphhanger or similar).

options.label: Google Fonts CSS link tag
options.description: Simplest. External request — breaks offline-first. Not viable for a PWA.

questions.title: Lucide icon package
questions.context: PRD §17: 'Lucide ONLY'. Need stroke-width 1.5px, sizes 18/20/24/28px. Bundle size matters for PWA cold start.

options.label: lucide-react
options.description: Recommended. Official React package; per-icon imports tree-shake; supports strokeWidth={1.5} per spec. Industry standard.

options.label: Inline SVG sprites generated from lucide-static
options.description: Zero JS for icons; one HTTP request. Build step needed to extract used icons. More setup.

options.label: @iconify/react with Lucide collection
options.description: Generic icon framework. Over-engineered for 'Lucide only'; larger runtime.

questions.title: Motion library
questions.context: PRD §17 motion: spring physics 120/18/1 (stiffness/damping/mass), capture-button 1.00→1.03→1.00 bounce, 3.2s breathing loop, 60ms cascade on lists, prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks. Animate via transform + opacity only.

options.label: motion (Framer Motion v12+, rebranded 2025)
options.description: Recommended. First-class spring physics matching PRD params; useReducedMotion hook; LayoutGroup for shared layout transitions; ~60kB gzipped. Largest community + most examples.

options.label: motion/react (subpath import)
options.description: Recommended. Same package (`motion`), but React consumers import from `motion/react` (or `motion/react-client` where required by RSC boundaries), never an ambiguous root import.

options.label: @motionone/react
options.description: Smaller bundle (~3kB), simpler spring API. Less spring-config flexibility for complex orchestration like 60ms cascade with shared dampers.

options.label: CSS @keyframes + custom JS spring helper
options.description: Minimal deps. Spring math by hand (or copy from react-spring source). Most control, most code, fewest deps.

questions.title: Spring physics constants location
questions.context: PRD locks: stiffness 120, damping 18, mass 1 across button press, sheet reveal, tab switch. Capture-button bounce 1.00→1.03→1.00. Breathing loop 1.00→1.02 over 3.2s ease-in-out. All consumers must read the same values.

options.label: src/shared/motion/springs.ts named exports
options.description: Recommended. Exports springs.primary, springs.captureBounce, springs.breathing consumed by transition={springs.primary}. Single source; covers extension for variants if added later.

options.label: Inline transition props in each consumer
options.description: Duplication; drift risk. Easy to read locally, hard to keep in sync.

options.label: Custom hook useSpringTransition(name)
options.description: Indirection without value. Same as (a) plus an unnecessary hook layer.

questions.title: Reduced-motion enforcement
questions.context: PRD §17: every animation has a reduced-motion fallback (shimmer → static, breathing → stop, cascade → 120ms fade, spring → 120ms linear, celebration → 200ms color tint). 'Motion is NEVER sole indicator of state change.' This must be enforceable so a future feature phase can't accidentally regress.

options.label: useReducedMotion() hook + Tailwind motion-reduce: variant + Stylelint CSS rule + ESLint TSX rule
options.description: Recommended. Distributed enforcement; catches runtime motion usage in React and CSS keyframes in stylesheets. CSS @keyframes enforcement belongs in Stylelint; ESLint covers TSX motion usage, emoji, and banned imports.

options.label: useReducedMotion() hook only — no CSS-level enforcement
options.description: Simpler. Misses CSS @keyframes which framer-motion's hook can't see.

options.label: Manual review only (no automated rule)
options.description: Risks regression in feature phases. PRs forget.

questions.title: Route transition strategy
questions.context: PRD §17: 'After route change, focus moves programmatically to main content region.' Tab switches preserve scroll per tab (UI-14). Next 16 ships experimental View Transitions API (unstable_ViewTransition) — opt-in fade between routes. This is orthogonal to button-press / sheet-reveal motion (Q-06) but governs the chrome of bottom-nav tab switches.

options.label: Static — no route transition animation; instant content swap + focus move
options.description: Recommended for MVP. Predictable, accessible, no spec-creep risk. Bottom-nav active indicator slides via CSS only (transform + opacity); content area swaps instantly.

options.label: Next 16 View Transitions API (unstable_ViewTransition)
options.description: Opt-in fade between routes; experimental API; reduced-motion via media query. Risks API churn. Can be retrofitted later if MVP feels too jumpy.

options.label: framer-motion LayoutGroup + AnimatePresence
options.description: Fade/slide via motion library; consistent with rest of motion system; more code; risk of layout-shift regressions on mobile.

questions.title: Headless component primitives library
questions.context: Need: dialog/modal sheet (focus trap, scrim, drag handle), toast region, dropdown, tabs (bottom-nav semantics). Must be a11y compliant from day 1. Affects every modal/menu in MVP. Phase 4 needs Modal sheet for T&C; Phase 6 for LGPD consent; Phase 7 for toxicity disclaimer.

options.label: @radix-ui/react-* primitives, excluding toast
options.description: Recommended. @radix-ui/react-dialog (modal sheet), @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu, @radix-ui/react-tabs. Toast ownership stays with Q-11 Sonner to avoid duplicate toast systems. Headless, fully a11y. Industry standard. Tree-shakes per primitive.

options.label: shadcn/ui (Radix + Tailwind preset components)
options.description: Generates code into your repo; tweakable. Pairs naturally if Tailwind chosen. More opinionated styling defaults to override.

options.label: Headless UI (@headlessui/react)
options.description: Tailwind Labs alt; smaller surface. No drag-handle bottom-sheet primitive — would need to build that piece manually.

options.label: Build all primitives from scratch
options.description: Full control, full a11y burden. High risk for an MVP under WCAG-AA-ship-blocker constraint.

questions.title: Toast / banner system
questions.context: Need: app-update toast (bottom, non-blocking, OFF-10), persistent offline banner (top, UI-24), discard summary toast (Phase 9), read-only banner (Phase 10), error toasts. Reduced-motion: instant fade. Per-message dismiss.

options.label: sonner
options.description: Recommended. Modern toast library, motion-friendly, ~3kB. Supports persistent + dismissible, Promise toasts, headless customization. Matches design discipline.

options.label: Radix UI Toast primitive + bespoke styling
options.description: Pairs naturally if Radix chosen for Q-10. Build the styled wrapper yourself; full design control.

options.label: react-hot-toast
options.description: Simpler API; less flexible for persistent banners; default styling needs heavy override.

options.label: Build from scratch on Radix Toast Region
options.description: More code; full design control; covers app-update + offline banner + ad-hoc toasts under one mental model.

questions.title: Dark mode toggle + flash prevention
questions.context: PRD §17: 'color-scheme: light dark', follow system, manual override in Settings. SSR-rendered Next 16 → if theme stored in localStorage, page paints with system pref then swaps to user choice = visible flash. Cookie read server-side avoids flash.

options.label: Cookie 'theme=auto|light|dark' read in root layout, sets <html data-theme='...'> SSR-side; Settings writes cookie via Server Action
options.description: Recommended. Zero flash for explicit light/dark override; works with edge runtime. For auto, render data-theme='auto' and let CSS media queries resolve system preference instead of SSR-guessing. Settings page (Phase 4) writes cookie; Phase 3 just reads. Server Action keeps Settings declarative.

options.label: localStorage + inline <script> in <head> reading before paint
options.description: Blocking script; classic anti-FOUC pattern. Works but smell. CSP-unfriendly (inline script needs nonce when CSP lands).

options.label: System pref only in Phase 3; manual override deferred to Phase 4
options.description: Simpler now. SC-1 implies dark mode is fully working in Phase 3 (cookie path proven end-to-end), so this risks back-pedaling.

questions.title: Settings → Theme override surface in Phase 3
questions.context: PRD §17 demands manual override 'in Settings'. Settings shell ships in Phase 4 (Account section). Phase 3 needs to prove the cookie+dark-mode contract works end-to-end. SC-1 implies the user-facing manual override exists.

options.label: Temporary toggle on Profile placeholder tab (Phase 3); Phase 4 moves into proper Settings → Account
options.description: Recommended. Proves the cookie+dark-mode contract; uses the design-system Toggle primitive. Phase 4 owns relocation.

options.label: Only system-pref dark mode in Phase 3; manual override deferred to Phase 4
options.description: Simpler. SC-1 'manual override' is met by the contract being live; surface deferred.

options.label: ?theme=dark URL param toggle in Phase 3 for testing; UI ships Phase 4
options.description: Debug-only path; ugly but unblocks Playwright snapshot tests of dark mode.

questions.title: Service worker offline strategy
questions.context: Phase 1 SW (src/app/sw.ts) is precache-only skeleton: precacheEntries: self.__SW_MANIFEST. PRD §10: 'Previously loaded catalog browsable offline; new identifications blocked.' Phase 9 owns offline queue. Phase 3's job: app-shell offline + static caching + API passthrough.

options.label: App-shell offline-first (HTML+JS+CSS precached) + StaleWhileRevalidate static + NetworkOnly /api/*
options.description: Recommended. Fast launch, predictable. Catalog data caching is Phase 5+ scope. Lets SW navigation handler serve the offline fallback when uncached.

options.label: Network-first navigation, fall back to /offline page on failure
options.description: Simpler but slower launch. Doesn't match PRD's 'previously loaded catalog browsable' promise.

options.label: Defer SW caching strategy entirely to Phase 9 (offline queue)
options.description: Phase 3 ships only manifest + register. OFF-09 / OFF-10 SC fail.

questions.title: Offline fallback page
questions.context: When user offline AND requests an uncached route. SC-4 mentions 'persistent offline banner' but doesn't define the offline fallback URL. The fallback IS one of the placeholder demo pages — exercises the empty-state primitive.

options.label: /offline static page composed of empty-state primitive (Sage line-art + Source Serif headline + Calm Slate hint + Canopy 'Tentar novamente' CTA)
options.description: Recommended. Proves empty-state primitive end-to-end, gives offline experience a brand-coherent surface. SW navigation handler serves it on uncached navigation when offline.

options.label: No dedicated offline page; rely only on persistent offline banner + browser default
options.description: Browser default 'You are offline' is ugly and English. Persistent banner appears on cached pages; uncached navigation still falls to browser.

options.label: Hard 'no offline mode in Phase 3' — disable SW navigation handler, defer to Phase 9
options.description: OFF-09 SC fails. Phase 5+ depends on this.

questions.title: App-update toast trigger mechanism
questions.context: OFF-10: detect new SW version waiting → bottom toast 'Nova versão disponível' + 'Atualizar' → tap fires skipWaiting + reload. Reduced-motion: instant fade. Never auto-reload mid-session. The mechanism connects SW lifecycle to the React toast system (Q-11).

options.label: Listen to Serwist registration events (onWaiting / onUpdated) → emit custom DOM event → toast component subscribes
options.description: Recommended. Serwist exposes hooks for this. Decoupled. Toast lives in app-group layout; SW lifecycle stays at registration site. Requires the service worker to stop using automatic skipWaiting/clientsClaim; the 'Atualizar' button sends the explicit skip-waiting message and then reloads.

options.label: Poll navigator.serviceWorker.controller + waiting registration manually
options.description: Verbose; no library hook needed. Robust against Serwist API changes.

options.label: @serwist/window register helper
options.description: Serwist's bundled client. Clean API; adds ~5kB. Worth it if it covers update-check + skipWaiting + claim cleanly.

questions.title: PWA icon set generation
questions.context: Manifest currently has zero icons. Phase 3 needs full set: 192/512 (Android), 180 (Apple touch), maskable variants, monochrome (Android adaptive), favicon. PRD demands brand-aligned theme color. Source SVG must come from founder or be a clear placeholder.

options.label: pwa-asset-generator from a single SVG source
options.description: Recommended. Automated, reproducible. Run as `pnpm icons:generate` script. CI never re-runs; outputs committed. Founder updates SVG → regenerate set.

options.label: Real Favicon Generator (online tool)
options.description: Manual one-time export. No CI reproducibility. OK if founder commits to one-and-done.

options.label: Hand-crafted in Figma / Sketch
options.description: Full control; founder-sourced. Time cost; no automation. Only works if founder owns design tooling.

questions.title: Manifest theme color value
questions.context: Current manifest sets theme_color: #FFFFFF — VIOLATES PRD §17 (no pure white). Theme color tints the browser chrome above the page (Android Chrome address bar, iOS PWA splash).

options.label: Paper Cream #FBF7EF (light) + Night Cream #1A1613 (dark) via two <meta name='theme-color' media='(prefers-color-scheme: …)'>
options.description: Recommended. Matches brand. iOS supports the media-query split since iOS 15; Android Chrome since 2022. Manifest theme_color = light value as fallback, and manifest background_color must also use Paper Cream instead of pure white.

options.label: Canopy Green #1F4D35 (single value)
options.description: Bolder; tints chrome the brand color. Some apps prefer this for brand recall.

options.label: Paper Cream only (no dark variant)
options.description: Simpler; iOS doesn't respect dark variants reliably anyway.

questions.title: PWA install prompt UX
questions.context: Phase 3 makes app installable. Choice: rely on browser default vs custom button. Custom prompts typically live in onboarding (Phase 4) or Settings. Phase 3's SC-1 is met by a visitor installing the PWA — doesn't require a custom button.

options.label: Browser default only — no custom prompt in Phase 3
options.description: Recommended. Simplest; meets SC-1 'a visitor installs the PWA'. Custom prompt revisited in Phase 4 onboarding if conversion data warrants.

options.label: Custom 'Instalar' button on Home empty state for unauthenticated visitors
options.description: More engagement; Home empty state is owned by Phase 5 — risk of bleed.

options.label: Capture beforeinstallprompt and surface a banner after first interaction
options.description: Most aggressive; risk of nag and brand-tone violation.

questions.title: Tablet-width centered container approach
questions.context: PROJECT.md: 'Mobile-first PWA, tablet-width centered on desktop (bg fills sides). No wide-screen design.' Need a max-width for the app shell. PRD §17 catalog grid breaks at 375 / 600 / 900 — implies tablet-class is in the design space.

options.label: Single root <div> with max-width: 480px centered, min-h-[100dvh]
options.description: Recommended. Phone-style centered; matches mobile-first ethos. Catalog 4-col layout still hits ≥900px viewports because grid is inside the container — but the container caps. Cleanest.

options.label: max-width: 600px container — gives tablet breathing room
options.description: More natural feel on iPad / desktop preview. Catalog 3-col fits cleanly (PRD breakpoint 600–899 = 3 cols). Slightly wider feel, still 'mobile shape'.

options.label: Per-route <Container> component with breakpoint-aware max-widths
options.description: Recommended. Keeps the default app shell phone-shaped while allowing routes with explicit PRD layout contracts, especially Catalog's 375/600/900 grid ladder, to opt into wider tablet-class content. Desktop side-fill remains Paper Cream / Night Cream.

questions.title: Bottom-nav routing structure
questions.context: UI-14: 4 tabs Home / Catálogo / Identificar / Perfil. PRD §17: 'Switching tabs preserves scroll + filter per tab. Never silently jumps to Home or resets.' Per-tab scroll preservation requires either parallel routes or manual save/restore.

options.label: Single layout + manual scrollY save/restore via sessionStorage in useLayoutEffect
options.description: Recommended for MVP. Simplest; works with App Router defaults; preserve via debounced scroll handler keyed by pathname. Low coupling.

options.label: Next 16 parallel routes (@home, @catalog, @identify, @profile) with persistent layout
options.description: Preserves DOM + scroll natively. Per Next 16 conventions; non-trivial setup; better UX for back/forward navigation. Refactor risk.

options.label: experimental.scrollRestoration + browser history API
options.description: Simplest; relies on browser history. Behavior less predictable for tab switches that aren't back/forward navigation.

questions.title: App shell layout group structure
questions.context: Bottom-nav lives only on app routes. Auth screens (Phase 4) and unverified-email blocker shouldn't show bottom-nav. Decision sets the route-group convention for the whole app.

options.label: Root layout has <html> + providers; route group (app) has bottom-nav layout; (auth) group has bare shell
options.description: Recommended. Phase 4 owns (auth); Phase 3 sets up (app) with bottom-nav. Clean separation; each group has its own layout boundary.

options.label: Single root layout with conditional bottom-nav based on route
options.description: Simpler now; harder to maintain as auth + admin + onboarding routes accumulate.

options.label: Defer route-group decision to Phase 4
options.description: Risks Phase 3 design contract breakage (unverified-email blocker test won't be possible).

questions.title: Per-tab scroll preservation pattern
questions.context: PRD §17 bottom-nav: 'Switching tabs preserves scroll + filter per tab. Never silently jumps to Home or resets.' Q-21 chose the routing structure; this is the explicit scroll-position policy.

options.label: Save scrollY to sessionStorage keyed by pathname on every scroll (debounced); restore on tab change in useLayoutEffect
options.description: Recommended. Survives navigation; resets on session. Works with any routing; ~30 LOC.

options.label: In-memory Map keyed by pathname (lost on reload)
options.description: Cheapest. Lost on tab close. Adequate for MVP if reload-resume isn't a goal.

options.label: Next 16 experimental.scrollRestoration
options.description: Browser-native; behavior less predictable for tab switches that aren't back/forward navigation. Pairs poorly with parallel routes if Q-21 chose them.

questions.title: Focus management on route change
questions.context: PRD §17: 'After route change, focus moves programmatically to main content region.' Tab order = visual reading order. SC-2 explicitly demands this for keyboard users.

options.label: usePathname listener in app-group layout calls mainRef.current?.focus(); main wrapper has tabIndex={-1} + aria-label
options.description: Recommended. Standard a11y pattern. Negative tabIndex makes <main> focusable without entering tab order. ARIA label says 'Conteúdo principal'.

options.label: Custom React Router-style focus library
options.description: Overkill for App Router; (a) is ~10 LOC.

options.label: Manual focus() calls per page
options.description: Drift; pages forget; SC-2 regression risk.

questions.title: Phase 3 composed primitives — multiSelect
questions.context: SC-4: 'Placeholder screens demonstrate every composed primitive.' Some primitives are general (button, empty state, error) — Phase 3 owns them. Others are feature-specific (toxicity badge, confidence ladder) — owning phase will build them. Pick all that ship in Phase 3.

options.label: Buttons (Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Destructive)
options.description: Recommended. PRD §17 specs all 4 variants; foundational; Phase 4+ all consume.

options.label: Inputs (TextInput / Select / Toggle) with §17 validate-on-blur + autocomplete contract
options.description: Recommended. Phase 4 signup is first consumer; Phase 3 ships pattern + behavior.

options.label: Modal sheet primitive (focus trap, scrim, drag handle, return focus)
options.description: Recommended. Phase 4 T&C reading + Phase 6 LGPD consent + Phase 7 toxicity disclaimer all need it.

options.label: Toast / banner system (app-update + persistent + inline error)
options.description: Recommended. OFF-10 + UI-19 + UI-24 all depend.

options.label: Skeleton / shimmer with 300ms delay + 120ms fade-in + reduced-motion fallback
options.description: Recommended. UI-17 mandatory in Phase 3.

options.label: Empty state composer (line-art + serif headline + slate hint + Canopy CTA)
options.description: Recommended. UI-18 mandatory in Phase 3. Used by /offline page + Phase 5 empty Catalog.

options.label: Inline calm error (UI-19 — never red wall, cause + recovery, retry path)
options.description: Recommended. UI-19 mandatory in Phase 3.

options.label: App-update toast (OFF-10)
options.description: Recommended. Specialization of toast-system. SC-5 mandatory.

options.label: Persistent offline banner
options.description: Recommended. UI-24 mandatory in Phase 3.

options.label: Capture button + breathing loop (PRD §17 circular 72px primitive + 3.2s 1.00→1.02 loop)
options.description: Recommended. SC-3 explicitly demands the breathing loop in Phase 3 even though Phase 6 is first to wire camera capture.

options.label: Generic card primitive (Warm Ivory base, 16px radius, L1 elevation)
options.description: Optional. Phase 5 plant card + Phase 7 care card extend; can ship the base now.

options.label: Confidence ladder (high/medium/low + redundant signals)
options.description: Skip. Phase 6 first uses; build then.

options.label: Toxicity badge (7-part composition)
options.description: Skip. Phase 7 first uses; build then.

options.label: Plant card (catalog 4:5 photo)
options.description: Skip. Phase 5 first uses.

options.label: Care card section (full-width with Hairline dividers)
options.description: Skip. Phase 7 first uses.

options.label: 'Gerado por IA' chip (Trust Teal pill)
options.description: Skip. Phase 7 first uses.

options.label: 'Cap atingido' chip (Overdue Rust pill)
options.description: Skip. Phase 6 first uses.

questions.title: Phase 3 placeholder pages
questions.context: SC-4: 'Placeholder screens demonstrate every composed primitive.' How much page structure ships in Phase 3?

options.label: 4 nav tabs as routes (/, /catalog, /identify, /profile) all showing thin placeholder empty states + bottom-nav routes between them + /offline page
options.description: Recommended. Exercises bottom-nav, empty state primitive, route-change focus, persistent offline banner. Each tab a thin placeholder. Phase 5+ replaces tab content.

options.label: Only Home (/) + a /playground route demoing every primitive
options.description: Less prod-shaped; primitives in one isolated place. Easier visual review.

options.label: Home + /offline only — bare minimum
options.description: Skips bottom-nav exercise. SC-2 hard to demonstrate.

options.label: Full Home empty state from §16 (capture button + 'Adicionar manualmente' link) + 3 stub tabs + /offline
options.description: Phase 3 ships UI-04 surface from §16, but UI-04 is mapped to Phase 5 in REQUIREMENTS. Bleeds into Phase 5 scope; risk.

questions.title: Skeleton primitive — bespoke or library
questions.context: PRD §17 skeleton: matches final geometry, 1.4s shimmer left-to-right, 300ms threshold (faster ops skip shimmer + fade content 120ms), reduced-motion → static block + 80ms fade. Cached responses skip shimmer entirely.

options.label: Bespoke <Skeleton> + <SkeletonGroup delay={300}> with CSS keyframes + motion-reduce: variant
options.description: Recommended. Full design control; 300ms gating via JS; ~80 LOC. Matches PRD spec exactly.

options.label: react-loading-skeleton library
options.description: Mature; styling override needed for design tokens; default shimmer is pulse — needs custom CSS to match PRD's left-to-right shimmer.

options.label: Tailwind animate-pulse only
options.description: Wrong motion (pulse, not shimmer). Violates PRD spec.

questions.title: i18n message file structure
questions.context: src/messages/pt-BR.json is currently empty ({}). Message keys grow rapidly. Two main structures: flat vs nested objects. next-intl supports both.

options.label: Nested by screen + component (home.empty.title, nav.tabs.catalog)
options.description: Recommended. next-intl useTranslations('home.empty') namespacing works naturally. Easier mental model as keys multiply.

options.label: Flat with kebab-case keys (home-empty-title)
options.description: Simpler tooling; no namespacing. Better for translation tools that expect flat keys.

options.label: Per-screen JSON files split (messages/home.json, messages/nav.json)
options.description: Premature for MVP scale. next-intl supports it via custom loader; maintenance overhead.

questions.title: Phase 3 translation depth
questions.context: Phase 3 only renders placeholder pages. How much pt-BR copy do we author? Established pattern carries forward. Translation tooling (e.g. machine pre-translation) is irrelevant — pt-BR-only at launch.

options.label: Full pt-BR strings for Phase 3 placeholders + design-system labels (~30-50 keys)
options.description: Recommended. Establishes the pattern; future phases extend. Includes nav labels, empty-state copy, app-update toast, offline banner, default error messages, focus-visible labels.

options.label: Minimal: just the strings rendered in Phase 3 placeholder screens (~10 keys)
options.description: Risks rework when Phase 4 lands more text. Pattern not fully exercised.

options.label: Stub keys with English fallback messages
options.description: Irrelevant — pt-BR-only at launch. Confuses the message contract.

questions.title: Offline banner detection mechanism
questions.context: UI-24 persistent offline banner. navigator.onLine is unreliable for captive portals (says online but no internet). Phase 1 ships a diagnostics endpoint at /api/v1/diagnostics/ping that returns 200.

options.label: useOnlineStatus hook combining navigator.onLine + window online/offline events + periodic /api/v1/diagnostics/ping heartbeat (e.g. 30s)
options.description: Recommended. Reliable across browsers and PWA edge cases (captive portal, intermittent). Heartbeat is cheap; backs off when offline. The GET ping endpoint must be production-safe and always return a cheap 200 response; it cannot remain gated to IDENTIFICATION_PROVIDER_MODE=stub.

options.label: navigator.onLine + window online/offline events only
options.description: Simpler; misses captive-portal case. Acceptable for MVP if heartbeat feels overengineered.

options.label: Service worker → page postMessage on fetch failures
options.description: Most accurate; complex coordination between SW and page. Reactive instead of proactive — banner appears only after a failed request.

questions.title: Read-only banner stub in Phase 3
questions.context: UI-24 mentions read-only banner. Subscription state machine ships Phase 10. Phase 3 just needs the banner component to RENDER when given a flag — Phase 10 wires the source.

options.label: Phase 3 builds banner component with prop-driven state; passes false everywhere; Phase 10 wires real subscription state
options.description: Recommended. Clean separation; primitive shipped; Phase 10 just provides the data.

options.label: Phase 3 renders the banner dev-only behind a query param for visual review
options.description: Useful for design QA; lives behind ?readonly=1. Easy to forget to remove.

options.label: Defer entirely to Phase 10
options.description: Phase 10 owns both component + wiring. Simpler scope for Phase 3 but requires Phase 10 to also do design work.

questions.title: Banned-pattern lint enforcement
questions.context: PRD §17 has dozens of 'banned' rules: no emoji, no pure black/white, no Inter, no glassmorphism, no gradient text, no 'Saiba mais' secondary CTAs in heroes. Manual review forgets. Lint-staged runs on every commit. SC-5 explicitly demands a 'design-system lint'.

options.label: Stylelint with custom rules + ESLint custom rule for emoji + Vitest snapshot rule for fonts
options.description: Recommended. Distributed enforcement — Stylelint catches color/typography/animation patterns; ESLint catches emoji + banned import patterns; Vitest snapshot covers cross-cutting checks.

options.label: Single Vitest rule scanning files for banned patterns
options.description: Central; can fail loudly in CI. Less granular feedback.

options.label: Manual review only via PRs
options.description: Fastest now, costliest at scale. SC-5 fails.

questions.title: Color contrast verification
questions.context: WCAG AA = ship blocker. PRD §17 lists hex contrast ratios per token (Canopy 9.1:1, Forest Ink 12.9:1, etc.). Phase 3 ships tokens — this is when to wire the gate.

options.label: Playwright + @axe-core/playwright on placeholder pages, both themes, both motion preferences, gating CI on violations
options.description: Recommended. Catches actual rendered contrast in real browser. Phase 1 already runs Playwright in CI. Snapshot the axe report for review.

options.label: axe-core unit tests against rendered components in JSDOM
options.description: Fast feedback loop; misses real CSS (pseudo-elements, custom properties via getComputedStyle inconsistencies).

options.label: One-time manual contrast-ledger test in Vitest
options.description: Checks tokens against expected ratios; catches hex-typo only. Skips real-page rendering.

questions.title: Visual regression testing
questions.context: Composed primitives + design system are visual contracts. Changes need review. Phase 3 establishes the regression baseline that all future phases extend.

options.label: Playwright snapshot tests for placeholder pages, both themes, both motion preferences
options.description: Recommended. Local screenshots committed; CI compares. Free; integrates with existing Playwright setup. Mask the date/time portions of formatted strings.

options.label: Chromatic / Percy via Storybook
options.description: Best UX for design QA; paid SaaS; setup heavy; needs Storybook (not in MVP).

options.label: No visual regression in Phase 3; rely on lint + axe + manual review
options.description: Risks brand drift over time; SC-5 'design-system lint' partially covers but not visual.

questions.title: Brand assets source
questions.context: Founder logo, Sage line-art illustrations for empty states, PWA icon source. PRD §17 demands custom illustrations 'NEVER stock photos, NEVER veranda scenes.' Source assets must exist before Phase 3 final review.

options.label: Founder provides SVG logo + 4–6 line-art illustrations before Phase 3 starts; placeholder SVGs ship if not
options.description: Recommended. Most realistic for greenfield. Phase 3 builds primitives; illustrations swap in trivially because Q-claude-discretion #3 (inline SVG with currentColor) keeps theme-aware.

options.label: Use Lucide outline icons only as illustration placeholders (no custom illustrations) until set is delivered
options.description: Empty-state primitive structure ships; illustration swap is trivial. Phase 3 success criteria don't gate on custom illustrations.

options.label: AI-generated line art (Midjourney / Recraft / etc.) — manual cleanup required
options.description: Risky brand voice; founder-sourced is principled. PRD bans AI clichés but illustrations themselves aren't banned per se.

options.label: Hand-coded SVG illustrations (founder or designer-authored)
options.description: Full control, full ownership; time cost.
